## Step 17 — Observed mass–redshift demographics of passive disks

This science section uses the frozen COSMOS2025 quantities, dual-passive definition
and native paired-band disk criteria. Artificial redshifting and morphology fitting
are separate validation work and are not run here. Original 39 cells/results remain
unchanged. The analysis is conditional on detected, eligible, morphology-measurable
galaxies; unknown morphology is retained in the denominator audit.

Original bin edges, a denominator-defined common-support rule, fixed reference
weights and uncertainty methods are documented in `mass_redshift_science_v1/ANALYSIS_PROTOCOL.md`.
Restart checks reject changed code, inputs or cached outputs. This section can run
in a fresh `phd` kernel independently of expensive preceding experiments.

from pathlib import Path
import os, sys, json

from IPython.display import display, Image, Markdown

from validate_passive_disk_mass_redshift import validate as validate_mass_redshift

print(json.dumps(summary, indent=2))
review = validate_mass_redshift(PROJECT, MASS_REDSHIFT)
print(review['status'])

### Step 17.1 — Joint counts, fractions and common support

Each cell reports eligible and measurable galaxies, passive/disk/passive-disk counts,
Wilson95% intervals, sparse-event flags and morphology-unknown bounds. The36
published marginal rows reconcile exactly. The primary joint decomposition has
mass10–11 support; PD/all alone also supports9.5–11 under an all-galaxy denominator
rule. The latter does not make low-mass/high-redshift disk/passive cells reliable.

### Step 17.2 — Fraction maps
Counts and Wilson95% intervals reveal actual support. Hatched cells have small denominators/events. These maps show observed conditional distributions, not intrinsic abundances.

### Step 17.3 — Fixed-mass and fixed-redshift comparisons
Low-mass PD/all declines strongly; the10.5–11interval does not show a uniform decline. Disk/passive fractions show strong mass dependence where passive counts support comparison. Curves are visual guides, not evolutionary tracks.

### Step 17.4 — Mass standardization and decomposition
Figure5 uses primary joint support10–11; the supplementary same-support comparison isolates mass-mix adjustment. A changing mass distribution alone does not explain the broader observed decline. Effective D/P is standardized PD/all divided by standardized P/all, preserving the product identity.

### Step 17.5 — Matched SFR–mass comparison
All403 disks have unique controls within0.1dex and0.1redshift. No significant matched ΔMS location or omnibus distribution contrast is established. Very low SED-model SFRs and floor flags are not direct upper limits or quenching timescales.

### Step 17.6 — Completeness, statistical validation and interpretation

The inherited mass floor lies above the conditional M/L diagnostic. This does
not validate detection completeness, morphology accuracy or intrinsic fractions.
Morphology eligibility, correlated mass/photoz errors, SED priors and cosmic
variance remain limitations. Deterministic coarse bins, quality/depth subsets,
fixed-label migration and SFR-floor sensitivities are recorded separately.
